text: Drake Maye put together perhaps his finest performance of the season in the Patriots' dominant 45-17 demolition of the Raiders at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, accounting for five total touchdowns and seemingly finding the confidence and deep ball that had eluded him early in the campaign—a particularly impressive feat given that New England was operating without its top receiver and both starting cornerbacks. The victory came with a significant price, however, as running back TreVeyon Henderson left the game with an ankle injury while left tackle Will Campbell suffered what NFL Network sources believe to be a knee sprain, adding to the mounting injury toll the Patriots have been absorbing. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's situation at his Monday presser, and the film review reveals not just Maye's commanding display but also a defense that proved stifling despite the personnel absences, suggesting that New England's ability to win convincingly in adverse circumstances might be the most encouraging sign of all.
